messages.subject: why different fit indices when using the ordered=true alone, and when using it with estimator="dwls""
parts:
hello dears,
I am testing a bifactor model for a scale using bifactor-CFA. i get different fit indices when adding the command ordered=true to the syntax without estimator="dwls". and when I put both together in the syntax. especially when I only use ordered=true I do not get robust fit indices. have a look at my output
which output should I take
please also mention if you spot any problem in the output


thank you in advance
dess,

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: why different fit indices when using the ordered=true alone, and when using it with estimator="dwls""
parts:
I believe it is safe to use only ordered = TRUE and let's lavaan set other options for us, as explained below in the last paragraph:

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

If we manually set the estimator (e.g., estimator = "DWLS"), then this overrides the default behavior and lavaan expects us to set other options, such as the methods used for the SEs (the "se" argument) and the model test statistics (the "test" argument). We can do this if we want to fully specify the methods to be used. Otherwise, let lavaan set them.

This is an illustration, showing the differences (some differences are also printed by summary(), e.g., in the section "Parameter Estimates:"):  Parameter Estimates:

``` r
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-17
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
dat <- HolzingerSwineford1939[, paste0("x", 1:9)]
dat <- scale(dat)
dat[dat > 0] <- 1
dat[dat <= 0] <- 0
dat <- as.data.frame(dat)

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit1 <- cfa(HS.model, data = dat, ordered = TRUE)
fit2 <- cfa(HS.model, data = dat, ordered = TRUE, estimator = "DWLS")

# Same estimator
lavInspect(fit1, "options")$estimator
#> [1] "DWLS"
lavInspect(fit2, "options")$estimator
#> [1] "DWLS"
# Robust test statistics only in fit1
names(lavInspect(fit1, "test"))
#> [1] "standard"       "scaled.shifted"
names(lavInspect(fit2, "test"))
#> [1] "standard"
# Different methods for standard errors
lavInspect(fit1, "options")$se
#> [1] "robust.sem"
lavInspect(fit2, "options")$se
#> [1] "standard"
```

<sup>Created on 2024-02-19 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

My two cents.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: why different fit indices when using the ordered=true alone, and when using it with estimator="dwls""
parts:
For model test statistics, we should read the column "scaled", that is, "YYY.YYY" in the following example.

Model Test User Model:
                                              Standard      Scaled
  Test Statistic                               XXX.XXX     YYY.YYY

For CFI and RMSEA, the *rows* labelled "robust" should be used. They only have one column each, though under "Scaled".

The release not for 0.6-13 may be relevant:

https://lavaan.ugent.be/history/dot6.html#version-0.6-13

Though the following thread is very old, it should still be applicable (except for the new versions of the statistics introduced in 0.6-13)

https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/6kiW0a_Y64A/m/O6lV_gCEAgAJ

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai
